scams.name: Melaka QR-Code Receipt Scam — Fake Payment Proof at Retailers
scams.description: Melaka's fastest-growing 2026 tourist-adjacent fraud is the falsified-QR-payment-receipt scam, where buyers show merchants a doctored DuitNow/Maybank/Touch 'n Go screenshot instead of actually paying. The canonical 2026 anchor is NST 'Fake QR receipts, real money: Couple's cheating spree ends in arrest' (April 21 2026, article 1423507) — a 25-year-old man and 32-year-old woman were detained in Melaka Tengah after hitting petrol stations and grocery stores for close to RM 3,000 in losses. thevibes.com 'Couple arrested in Melaka over QR code receipt scam targeting retailers' (article 122138, 2026) gives the same arrest pattern, and NST 'Trader cheated of RM 25,270 in QR code Harumanis scam' (April 2026, article 1421289) shows how much larger the losses run when the merchants themselves get conned. Community reports also document the 2025-2026 QR surge, the broader fake-screenshot ecosystem in Malaysia, and first-person accounts of potential scam attempts. The 2026 scam layer for tourists: (a) bogus QR stickers pasted over legitimate table-side payment codes in Jonker Street food stalls and 7-Eleven outlets — you scan, pay, and the RM 35 goes to a mule account while the vendor never sees it; (b) forged 'payment successful' screenshots shown at snack stalls, batik shops, and durian vendors — cashiers in a rush (especially at the Friday-Sunday night-market peak) wave you through; (c) fake DuitNow receipt apps generating pixel-perfect confirmations with spoofed reference numbers; (d) 'help me pay, my card won't work' approach where a stranger asks you to DuitNow-transfer for them, offering cash back — the cash is counterfeit and your transfer is real; (e) QR-sticker swaps at Taman Rempah river-cruise ticket counter and Menara Taming Sari kiosks targeting non-Malaysian-card-holders confused about DuitNow. For travelers: (1) ALWAYS verify the payee name on your banking app before tapping confirm — a legitimate Jonker Walk food stall will show the registered business or owner's full Malay name, not an unrelated personal account; (2) pay in cash (RM 10 / RM 20 notes) for every stall transaction under RM 50 — keeps the fraud surface near zero; (3) if a stranger asks you to DuitNow-transfer on their behalf for cash, REFUSE — community reports confirm this is always a scam; (4) peel back any QR sticker that looks freshly stuck or slightly misaligned — legitimate stickers are usually laminated behind plastic; (5) take a photo of the QR decal before scanning at stalls you're unsure about so your bank can trace a dispute; (6) NEVER accept a screenshot as proof of incoming payment — only a real-time push notification on your own bank app counts; (7) report suspicious QR stickers to MBMB enforcement or the vendor's parent chain (7-Eleven, KK Super Mart, Caltex); (8) save the National Scam Response Centre hotline 997 and MOTAC tourist line 1300-88-5050 for immediate freezes.
scams.avoidance: Verify payee name on banking app before confirming — not just the amount Pay cash (RM 10 / RM 20) for stall transactions under RM 50 NEVER DuitNow-transfer on behalf of a stranger offering 'cash back' Peel-test QR stickers that look freshly stuck — legitimate ones are laminated Only a push notification on your own bank app is real proof of payment National Scam Response Centre 997; MOTAC tourist line 1300-88-5050
scams.location: Jonker Street/Walk night-market stalls, 7-Eleven & KK Super Mart outlets across Melaka Tengah, petrol stations, Taman Rempah jetty ticket counter, Menara Taming Sari, Dataran Pahlawan food court, Mahkota Parade retail

scams.name: Melaka Trishaw (Beca) Bait-and-Switch Overcharge
scams.description: Melaka's LED-bedecked, music-blaring Hello Kitty / Pikachu / Elsa trishaws are the single most-photographed symbol of the UNESCO zone — and also the city's most-documented 2026 tourist-overcharge. The canonical 2026 anchor is The Star 'Melaka looks into claims of trishaw rider overcharging tourist' (April 15 2026) — Majlis Bandaraya Melaka Bersejarah (MBMB) launched a probe after a Threads user 'Yasmin_aishah' posted that her husband was quoted RM 50 and then billed RM 80 at the end of a short heritage-loop ride; MBMB reaffirmed the OFFICIAL FARE is RM 25–RM 50 depending on route. WeirdKaya 'M'sian Woman Claims Trishaw Rider Demanded RM 80 For Ride In Melaka' (April 15 2026) is the parallel incident write-up, and The Star 'A digital revolution ahead for Melaka's trishaws' (January 3 2025) documents the ongoing digitisation push explicitly aimed at ending fare disputes. Community reports add local colour: 'RM 30 for a trishaw ride is standard; what do you want with music and lights? Go to Melaka then pay RM 50.' Broader community threads on Melaka trishaws and the local trishaw culture, plus Tripadvisor 'Tourist trap — Malacca Trishaw Service' reviews, corroborate the bait-and-switch pattern. The 2026 scam layer: (a) rider quotes RM 30–RM 50 at the Stadthuys/Red Square (Dutch Square) taxi stand, then demands RM 80–RM 150 on arrival claiming 'per person', 'extra for photo stops', or 'extra for music'; (b) 'free photo at Christ Church' tacked on at RM 20 per shot; (c) short 10-minute loops marketed as '1 hour tour' that circle the same block three times; (d) airport-style 'fuel surcharge' or 'MBMB permit fee' invented on the spot; (e) card-only riders with POS terminals running DCC (dynamic currency conversion) adding 10-15%; (f) some Hello Kitty / Pikachu riders around Jonker Walk Friday-night market quoting RM 100 flat for a 3-block hop. For travelers: (1) MBMB OFFICIAL FARE is RM 25–RM 50 depending on route per The Star 'Melaka looks into claims' (April 15 2026) — ANY quote above RM 50 for a standard Stadthuys-to-Jonker loop is overcharging; (2) AGREE the total fare and route in writing (photo of riders' fare card OR WhatsApp screenshot) BEFORE boarding; (3) confirm 'total, not per person' — 'Jumlah semua, bukan satu orang?'; (4) if overcharged on arrival, pay the agreed amount in cash, step away, and photograph the rider + trishaw number plate; (5) report disputes to MBMB enforcement (06-282 9804) or Tourism Malaysia hotline 1300-88-5050 — MBMB confirmed monitoring in April 2026; (6) the Hello Kitty / Pikachu trishaws are ALL legitimate licensed vehicles but pricing varies wildly between riders — shop 2-3 before boarding; (7) Grab is fine across Melaka for RM 8–RM 15 hotel-to-Jonker trips — use it for practical transport and reserve trishaws for one decorative photo-loop; (8) save 'RM 25–RM 50, MBMB kadar rasmi' (official rate) on your phone translator to show disputatious riders.
scams.avoidance: MBMB official fare RM 25–RM 50 — anything above RM 50 for Stadthuys-to-Jonker loop is overcharging Agree total fare in writing (photo of fare card) BEFORE boarding Confirm 'Jumlah semua, bukan satu orang?' (total, not per person) Photograph rider + trishaw number plate if disputed on arrival Report to MBMB 06-282 9804 or Tourism Malaysia 1300-88-5050 Grab is RM 8–RM 15 for normal transport; use trishaws for photo-loops only
scams.location: Stadthuys / Red Square (Dutch Square) trishaw stand, Jonker Street / Jonker Walk night market entrance (Fri-Sun), Christ Church Melaka plaza, A'Famosa / St. Paul's Hill loop, Menara Taming Sari drop-off

scams.name: Jonker Street Night-Market Food & Durian Overcharge
scams.description: Jonker Street / Jonker Walk night market (Friday 6 PM-midnight, Saturday-Sunday) is Melaka's headline tourist dining strip and the city's most-documented 2024-2026 food-overcharge zone. One traveler wrote: 'All scams start out gentle so you go okay okay okay, then when the final big scam comes in, also okay! Then after kena scam you scratch head.' Another first-person 2025 anchor involves a Dutch tourist who arrived in Melaka and was scammed within hours. Community reports cover broader Malaysia-wide scam context, 2025 meta-discussion on tourist scams, and thesun.my 'M'sian pays RM 2.50 for one curry puff, gets almost no filling' (2025) documenting the per-item-markup pattern. The 2026 scam layer: (a) menu-less stalls quoting 'market price' then charging RM 35–RM 50 for a plate of fried rice that should cost RM 10–RM 15; (b) satay celup per-stick confusion — legitimate rate is RM 1–RM 1.30 per stick at Capitol Satay, tourist stalls charge RM 3–RM 5 per stick without announcing and dip sticks for you unsolicited; (c) durian per-kg vs per-piece confusion — a Musang King is quoted 'RM 80/kg' but weighed with husk at 2 kg for a RM 160 charge when the flesh is 300g; community durian threads consistently document this; (d) 'live cooking demo' satay stalls sneaking extra skewers onto your plate then billing by count; (e) bundled 'tourist combo' at RM 120 where each item individually costs RM 8–RM 15; (f) uncovered drinks (sugarcane, cendol, ais kacang) charged at RM 15–RM 20 vs the RM 5–RM 8 local rate; (g) Hokkien mee 'large portion' upsell from RM 8 to RM 35. For travelers: (1) refuse any stall without a VISIBLE printed price list — Melaka licensed stalls are required to display prices and MBMB enforcement actively ticket non-compliant vendors; (2) ask 'berapa semua?' (how much in total?) BEFORE ordering, not after — confirm per-piece or per-kg for durian specifically; (3) durian: weigh the WHOLE fruit with husk only if buying the whole fruit; if paying by flesh weight, insist the seller cut and weigh the flesh in front of you; (4) satay celup: check the per-stick rate on the wall board before dipping — Capitol Satay and McQuek's both post RM 1–RM 1.30 per stick; (5) take a photo of the menu/price board BEFORE ordering in case of dispute; (6) cap any stall meal at RM 15–RM 20 per person for street food — anything higher indicates you're in a tourist-trap stall; (7) Jonker Walk is busy Fri-Sun only — weekday dining at Kocik Kitchen, Baba Charlie, or Bunga Raya food court offers honest pricing; (8) if overcharged, pay what you agreed + walk — refuse shouted 'extras', photograph the stall and report to MBMB hotline 06-282 9804 or Tourism Malaysia 1300-88-5050.
scams.avoidance: Refuse stalls without a VISIBLE printed price list — MBMB requires display Confirm per-piece OR per-kg for durian — weigh flesh in front of you Satay celup: check per-stick rate on wall board (legitimate RM 1–RM 1.30) Photo the price board BEFORE ordering; ask 'berapa semua?' up front Cap stall meals at RM 15–RM 20 per person for street food MBMB hotline 06-282 9804; Tourism Malaysia 1300-88-5050
scams.location: Jonker Street / Jonker Walk night market (Jalan Hang Jebat) Friday-Sunday, Jonker Street Hawker Centre, durian stalls along Jalan Tokong, roast-duck stalls at the Jonker Walk entrance, satay celup strip near Kampung Banda Kaba

scams.name: Melaka River Cruise Unofficial-Ticket & Tout Overcharge
scams.description: The Melaka River Cruise is the UNESCO zone's flagship paid attraction — a 45-minute 9 km loop on the Melaka River departing from Taman Rempah (Jalan Persisiran Bunga Raya) and Dataran Muara Sungai Melaka jetties — and is surrounded by a persistent 2024-2026 unofficial-ticket-seller ecosystem targeting confused arrivals. Per malaysia.travel / visitmelaka.com.my and Trip.com the OFFICIAL FOREIGNER ADULT FARE is RM 30 (RM 25 MyKad local) with RM 15 child and RM 15 disabled; senior 60-69 RM 28 via TheSmartLocal. Community reports cover 2025 first-person planning for the Melaka River Cruise, the Dutch-tourist anchor about being intercepted before reaching legitimate counters, broader cataloguing of the tout pattern, and active local moderation of Melaka-area scam alerts. The 2026 scam layer: (a) touts standing outside both Taman Rempah and Muara jetties quoting RM 50–RM 80 per adult for 'VIP skip-the-line' tickets when the OFFICIAL rate is RM 30; (b) hand-held printed vouchers sold at cafes along Jalan Laksamana Cheng Ho that turn out to be expired Klook screenshots or forged QR codes; (c) 'combined cruise + Taming Sari tower + trishaw' packages at RM 150–RM 200 where each element can be bought officially for a fraction; (d) hotel-desk 'concierge' upsells at RM 90/adult with the hotel pocketing a RM 60 tout margin; (e) 'cruise is sold out, take my private boat for RM 100' fake-scarcity sell at the jetty bench area; (f) unlicensed QR decals on benches near the Taman Rempah ticket office redirecting to phishing pages that harvest card details (ties directly to the 2026 QR-code scam in this city); (g) Grab drivers diverted to 'unofficial jetty' addresses 10 minutes away. For travelers: (1) OFFICIAL fares: foreign adult RM 30, MyKad adult RM 25, child RM 15, senior 60-69 approx RM 28 — buy ONLY at the posted ticket counters at Jeti Taman Rempah or Dataran Muara Sungai Melaka, OR online at ticket.melakarivercruise.my; (2) IGNORE every tout offering 'VIP' / 'skip-the-line' / 'better boat' — the only boats are the official blue-and-white Melaka River Cruise fleet; (3) refuse hotel-desk cruise resales unless the total quoted matches RM 30 x adults exactly; (4) the cruise runs 09:00-23:00 daily and rarely sells out except during school holidays — 'sold out' pressure is almost always fake; (5) approach the Taman Rempah jetty via the OFFICIAL entrance off Jalan Persisiran Bunga Raya, not side alleys; (6) verify Klook / GetYourGuide / Trip.com QR vouchers on the app ONLY — never trust a printed PDF handed to you on the street; (7) if overcharged at a tout, pay nothing until you reach the OFFICIAL counter and can confirm posted rates; (8) report unlicensed ticket sales to MBMB enforcement, Taman Rempah Jetty 06-286 1530, or Muara Jetty 06-286 1531; save Tourism Malaysia 1300-88-5050.
scams.avoidance: Official fares foreign adult RM 30 / MyKad RM 25 / child RM 15 — buy ONLY at posted counters or ticket.melakarivercruise.my IGNORE all touts offering 'VIP' / 'skip-the-line' / 'better boat' — the fleet is uniform blue-and-white Refuse hotel-desk resales above RM 30/adult; refuse street-vendor PDF vouchers Cruise rarely sells out — 'sold out' pressure is almost always fake Approach Taman Rempah via Jalan Persisiran Bunga Raya, not side alleys Taman Rempah 06-286 1530; Muara 06-286 1531; Tourism Malaysia 1300-88-5050
scams.location: Jeti Taman Rempah (Jalan Persisiran Bunga Raya, 75100 Melaka), Dataran Muara Sungai Melaka jetty, tout approaches along Jalan Laksamana Cheng Ho, hotel concierge desks in Banda Hilir, Grab drop-off decoys near Kampung Morten

scams.name: Melaka Costumed-Character Beggar (Spider-Man/Frog) & Child-Exploitation Scam
scams.description: Melaka's heritage zone hosts one of Malaysia's most-documented 2025-2026 child-exploitation-via-costumed-begging schemes, which exploded into national news in February 2026. The canonical 2026 anchor is The Star ''Spider-Man' suspect investigated for using young girl to beg in Melaka' (February 9 2026) — authorities intercepted an adult in a Spider-Man costume operating alongside a 7-year-old girl from Terengganu, also in Spider-Man costume, soliciting money from tourists in the heritage area. Rakyat Post 'Authorities Intercept Spider-Man And Spider-Girl In Melaka Over Alleged Child Exploitation' (February 10 2026) gives the Kalsom enforcement-intervention detail; Bernama ''Spiderman' Viral Video: Mum Says Unaware Daughter Was Begging' (February 11 2026, id 2523015) is the mother's response; thesun.my 'Melaka mother denies knowledge of daughter's Spiderman begging' (2026) is the parallel anchor; SCMP ''Spider-Man' beggar with girl sparks Malaysia child exploitation probe' (article 3342986) is the international pick-up. Community reports cover the 2026 Spider-Man case in detail. The pattern predates Spider-Man: earlier community reports document frog-costumed beggar round-ups, and a Dutch-tourist 2025 anchor references the 'fake wound scam' distraction pattern overlapping here. The 2026 scam layer: (a) adult in Spider-Man / Elsa / Pikachu / frog costume positioned near Christ Church, Stadthuys / Red Square, and Jonker Street entrance with a child (often not their own) in matching costume posing for photos; (b) after the photo, an aggressive 'RM 20 per person' tip demand — crowd pressure tips at RM 50–RM 100; (c) child handles the cash collection while the adult manages positioning — classic exploitation layering; (d) distraction overlap — while one handler engages the tourist, a second approaches from behind and pickpockets or lifts phones from cafe tables; (e) 'fake-wound' beggars on Jalan Hang Jebat and along the river walk using theatrical injuries to extract RM 10–RM 50; (f) roving beggars at Dataran Pahlawan with disability-theatre scripts. For travelers: (1) NEVER pay a costumed character for a photo in Melaka without a posted rate card — MBMB-licensed buskers at the Stadthuys display fixed tips of RM 2–RM 5, not RM 20–RM 100; (2) if a costumed adult is working alongside a young child soliciting money, WALK AWAY and report immediately to MBMB (06-282 9804) or Melaka Tengah District Police Chief's office (Polis Bantuan Kalsom, in charge of 2026 child-exploitation cases); (3) do NOT take the photo in the first place — posing triggers the demand; (4) legitimate Melaka heritage-zone buskers operate within the Dataran Pahlawan / Stadthuys permit zone with visible MBMB badges — outside that zone they are unlicensed; (5) if you want to support a child in need, donate via UNICEF Malaysia or Yayasan Chow Kit rather than cash to street handlers who may be controllers; (6) emergency 999; child-exploitation reporting via Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat (JKM) 15999; (7) keep phones in zipped bags — community reports flag the costumed-character photo moment as a common phone-snatch prelude; (8) if you witness a probable-exploitation case, photograph the scene (from distance) and submit to MBMB enforcement — direct police reports in February 2026 led to the Spider-Man interception.
scams.avoidance: NEVER pay costumed characters without a POSTED rate card — licensed Melaka buskers display RM 2–RM 5 tips only Do NOT pose for the photo in the first place — it triggers the demand If an adult is working with a young child for donations, walk away + report MBMB enforcement 06-282 9804; JKM child-welfare line 15999 Donate via UNICEF Malaysia / Yayasan Chow Kit — NOT cash to street handlers Keep phones in zipped bags — costumed-character photos are phone-snatch preludes
scams.location: Christ Church Melaka plaza, Stadthuys / Red Square (Dutch Square), Jonker Street / Jonker Walk entrance, Dataran Pahlawan, A'Famosa fort steps, river walk along Jalan Laksamana

scams.name: Melaka Fake-Donation & Charity-Solicitor Scam
scams.description: Melaka's UNESCO heritage zone — with its religious-architecture density (Christ Church, St. Paul's Hill, Kampung Kling Mosque, Cheng Hoon Teng Temple, Hang Li Poh's Well) — has become a 2024-2026 hotbed for unsolicited 'charity donation' approaches weaponising tourist goodwill. The canonical April 2026 anchor is FMT 'Fake fundraising appeal circulating on WhatsApp, Melaka cops warn' (April 22 2026) — Melaka state police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar explicitly denies police are organising any fundraising and warns the public. NST 'Melaka police track scammers using department's name to solicit donations' (April 22 2026, article 1423890) gives the parallel 'PDRM name misuse' pattern — scammers impersonating police or religious departments to collect 'building funds'. thevibes.com 'Man arrested for charity scam using fake Islamic department letterhead in Penang' (article 114157) documents the Peninsular Malaysia-wide pattern. Community reports also cover a 2025 Dutch-tourist anchor where a stranger in a Singapore shirt runs a 'help me with family emergency' donation-adjacent script, the guilt-trip street-approach baseline, and the broader Malaysia fraud pattern. The 2026 scam layer: (a) hand-held 'mosque/temple building fund' clipboards at Christ Church plaza, Kampung Kling Mosque, and Cheng Hoon Teng Temple with laminated 'photographs' and 'receipts' — real religious institutions in Malaysia do NOT solicit cash from tourists on the street; (b) 'deaf-mute' or fake-disability script where the solicitor hands a laminated card asking for RM 50–RM 100 and pushes until you either pay or walk off; (c) 'orphanage visit — donate RM 200 for children's meals' packaged with a fake tour; (d) WhatsApp-broadcast fundraising links impersonating PDRM Melaka or JAKIM per FMT (April 22 2026) and NST (April 22 2026, article 1423890); (e) 'flood relief' or 'fire relief' street collectors with photocopied 'approval letters' — always fake — ramping up after any local or regional incident; (f) QR-code sticker donation boxes in front of A'Famosa fort linked to mule accounts rather than any registered charity; (g) 'help my stranded family' scripts targeting foreign tourists near Mahkota Parade. For travelers: (1) NEVER give cash to a street solicitor in Melaka — legitimate Malaysian religious and charitable collections happen inside religious buildings with registered permit numbers (Rumah Ibadat / JAKIM / MBMB), NOT on the sidewalk; (2) if pressed, politely say 'Saya tak bagi — telefon polis' (I don't give — call the police) and walk — scammers de-escalate at the mention of PDRM; (3) the Melaka state police chief (Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar, April 2026) has publicly stated PDRM runs NO public fundraising — any WhatsApp / clipboard / QR code appealing 'for PDRM' is fraud; (4) to actually give, use only registered charities: Yayasan Chow Kit, MERCY Malaysia, Tabung Haji, UNICEF Malaysia — all with transparent online payment portals; (5) refuse every 'deaf-mute' clipboard approach — the laminated card is a known scam template across Peninsular Malaysia; (6) report street solicitors to MBMB enforcement 06-282 9804 or Melaka police 999; (7) WhatsApp forwards claiming 'help Melaka flood victims' should be verified against PDRM's official Facebook (Polis Melaka) before ANY transfer — per FMT (April 22 2026); (8) never scan QR codes on roadside donation boxes — most are spoofed to mule accounts per the NST April 2026 advisory.
scams.avoidance: NEVER give cash to street solicitors — legitimate Malaysian charities collect inside buildings with permit numbers 'Saya tak bagi — telefon polis' (I don't give — call the police) and walk PDRM Melaka runs NO public fundraising (Dzulkhairi Mukhtar, April 2026) Registered charities only: MERCY Malaysia, UNICEF Malaysia, Tabung Haji Refuse 'deaf-mute' clipboard approaches — a known Peninsular template Verify any WhatsApp appeal via official Polis Melaka Facebook before transferring
scams.location: Christ Church Melaka plaza, St. Paul's Hill, Kampung Kling Mosque, Cheng Hoon Teng Temple (Harmony Street), A'Famosa fort entrance, Mahkota Parade, Dataran Pahlawan, Melaka Sentral bus terminal, Jonker Walk entrance
